newsitem.title: KUWAIT: KPC says long-term sales ease impact of price fall.
newsitem.headline: KPC says long-term sales ease impact of price fall.

text.p: Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) said on Monday the current crude oil price fall has had no impact on its market share, thanks to a marketing policy that depends largely on long-term deals, the Kuwait News Agency reported.
"KPC affirmed today (Monday) it has not lost any markets due to a fall in crude oil prices," the official agency said.
"Long-term contracts make more than 95 percent of total (KPC) sales," it quoted KPC's managing director for marketing, Hani Hussein, as saying.
"KPC is keen on reducing sales in spot markets to the least amount possible" in view of weak prices, he added.
World benchmark Brent crude future have slumped this year from just below $25 a barrel in early January to $17.54 on Thursday, the lowest in nearly 10 months.
Asked about measures that KPC might adopt to escape losses from weaker oil prices, Hussein said KPC wsa considering involvement in joint refinery projects and building storage tankers.
"KPC adopts a policy based on diversifying crude oil markets in various parts of the world, with (special) focus on promising markets in terms of expected rise in demand," added Hussien.
Hussein said the oil prices fall was a "correction move" following 1996 price rises to levels unmatched in years.
Hussein blamed the fall in oil prices on increased oil output particularly by North Sea producers, warmer than expected weather and renewed Iraqi oil exports.
Kuwait produces about two million barrels per day. Oil makes about 90 percent of the desert state's revenue.
